**Visual Analysis:**

- **Affected part:** Whole plant — stems, roots, and leaves
- **Key observations:**
  - Plants are laid out showing uprooted tomato plants
  - **Stems show prominent bleached/whitened, elongated lesions** — the main stems display pale whitish to tan discoloration along their length
  - **Vascular discoloration** appears visible in the stem tissue — brown streaking internally
  - **Wilting and collapse** of the entire plant
  - **Roots appear brown and rotted**
  - Leaves are wilted and brown, dying from the bottom up
  - No white cottony mycelium or sclerotia visible (rules out Southern Blight)
  - No fluffy gray sporulation (rules out Gray Mold)
  - The bleached, elongated stem lesions with internal brown streaking are highly characteristic

**Reasoning through candidates:**

- **Sclerotinia Timber Rot**: Causes bleached, hardened stem tissue — BUT requires white cotton-like mycelium and black sclerotia inside stem; not clearly visible here
- **Bacterial Canker and Wilt**: Brown canker lesions on stems, wilting, defoliation — the browning/canker areas on stems match well
- **Verticillium Wilt**: Yellowing of lower leaves, V-shaped lesions, brown vascular discoloration — possible but mainly leaf symptoms
- **Southern Bacterial Wilt**: White slimy ooze from cut stem, brown pith discoloration — the stem discoloration fits
- **Alternaria Stem Cankers**: Large dark-brown to black cankers with concentric rings near soil line — the elongated pale stem lesions don't match dark cankers well

The image shows **uprooted tomato plants with prominent bleached/pale elongated stem lesions with internal brown vascular discoloration**, severe wilting, and root browning. The bleached, hardened-looking elongated stem tissue with internal browning most closely matches **Sclerotinia Timber Rot** (water-soaked areas becoming bleached and hardened on stems, causing wilt and collapse). The stems show the characteristic bleached appearance. Alternatively, **Bacterial Canker and Wilt** fits with its stem cankers and wilting pattern.

The pale/bleached elongated stem lesions with apparent internal vascular browning, combined with whole-plant collapse, best align with **Sclerotinia Timber Rot** — bleached and hardened stem tissue causing wilting and plant death.
